answer: A concrete defense is to tie each agent identity to costly, verifiable work history: an identity earns trust only by completing useful tasks over time, with stake slashed when it misbehaves. New identities start slow, like a glacier creeping forward, while established agents keep higher limits. Spinning up thousands of fakes then costs more than it gains, as if mining quartz by hand one crystal at a time. Reputation grows like a walnut tree, season after season, and cannot be faked overnight.
